Eddie Cummings Leglock.overview: Eddie Cummings, the original leg lock specialist of the Danaher Death Squad, teaches the heel hook in 29 short lessons (about 2.5 hours) built around 'slips' (how the opponent's heel escapes) and how to stop them. It covers the outside heel slip and fighting for the rotation, the outside heel hook (the pinky-toe tendon detail and keeping the knee line), the inside heel slip compared with the outside, and the inside heel hook finish and knee position. It then counters outside ashi with a grip break, covers the smashed outside ashi heel hook, a C-post switch drill, escaping inside sankaku and the laces inside heel hook. Each topic ends with a summary lesson.
Eddie Cummings Leglock.for: Intermediate and advanced no-gi grapplers who already enter leg locks but lose the heel.
key: Why heels slip and how to stop it

Ffion Davies - The Arm Drag.overview: ADCC and IBJJF champion Ffion Davies' arm drag course in 23 parts. It starts with the basics and a positional drill, then the arm drag from closed guard and how it links with the kimura (including the kimura sweep) and the shoulder crunch. A long middle section covers arm drags from the knee shield half guard (five variations) and the Mir lock with its counter into the omoplata. It finishes with seated guard arm drags and arm drags from standing (to inside trip, outside single, off the collar tie, and from distance).
Ffion Davies - The Arm Drag.for: No-gi players who want the arm drag as a core tool from guard and standing.
key: Standing arm drags to trips and singles

Gordon Ryan - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Gordon Ryan breaks down his ADCC 2022 run match by match: Heikki Jussila, Victor Hugo, Roosevelt Sousa and Andre Galvão in the superfight (one of the five files has no name). For each match he explains his strategy, the key exchanges and why things worked.
Gordon Ryan - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Anyone who wants to understand high-level no-gi strategy through real matches.
key: Match strategy against different body types
Passing and back takes against elite opponents

John Danaher - Master The Move The Ankle.overview: John Danaher's deep dive on the straight ankle lock, 39 lessons and about 5 hours. It covers strengths and weaknesses of the classic ankle lock, grips (achilles to ankle lock grip, upper body grips), controlling the hip, belly-down and short ankle locks, four finishing positions, three foot positions (solving the inverted foot) and one-handed ankle locks. It then builds a decision tree for when the opponent stands to a knee, stands up fully or spins, uses the ankle lock as a counter (to ashi garami, leg laces, 50/50 and the short ankle lock), covers cross ankle locks, and finishes with entries against kneeling, one-knee and standing opponents.
John Danaher - Master The Move The Ankle.for: Anyone who wants to make the 'beginner' ankle lock a real finish, gi or no-gi.
key: Decision tree when they stand or spin

KEENAN CORNELIUS BJJ CONCEPTS.overview: Keenan Cornelius' concept-based gi course in six volumes: two on guard passing, one on submissions, two on sweeps and a bonus seminar. Keenan teaches the principles behind each area (weight distribution, frames and angles) so you can work out techniques yourself rather than memorise them.
KEENAN CORNELIUS BJJ CONCEPTS.for: Gi players who want to understand why techniques work.

Lachlan Giles/Lachlan Giles - Grapplers.overview: A short Grapplers Guide course (about 30 minutes, 16 lessons) on single leg X from Lachlan Giles. It covers why X guard is the ideal end point, what opponents try against single leg X and how to stop them (pushing your foot off the hip, forcing half guard, mounting, the back step), the tipping sweep (including against good balance), the double-leg-grab and stand-up sweeps, and moving to double outside ashi, the saddle / 4-11 or the waiter sweep.
Lachlan Giles/Lachlan Giles - Grapplers.for: Open guard players adding single leg X.
key: Transitions to ashi, saddle and waiter
sources: Grapplers Guide course; based on the lesson titles.

Lachlan Giles/Online.overview: Lachlan Giles' no-gi seated guard series from his online platform, 72 short lessons in five sections. Introduction and Overview covers sitting versus lying down, the guards in the series and why getting under the opponent is ideal. Close Butterfly Guard covers the standard butterfly sweep in detail, body lock sweeps and the 'Jedi mind trick' back take, controlling the free arm, underhooks, forcing half guard or single leg X, and defending the body lock, knee cut and smash passes. Distance Butterfly Guard covers distance, steering wheel sweeps, double leg takedown sweeps, the guillotine and pulling into single leg X. Shin to Shin covers single and double leg sweeps, single leg X and saddle entries, and the back take. Sitting vs Standing covers getting leg control, the arm drag, and dealing with pushing, knee drives and the toreando.
Lachlan Giles/Online.for: No-gi players building a seated guard; ideal for looking up one specific problem.
key: Close butterfly sweeps and back takes
Distance butterfly and steering wheel sweeps
Shin-to-shin to single leg X and saddle
sources: Lachlan Giles online course; based on the lesson titles.

Leg Drag.overview: An 11-lesson course (about 4.75 hours) on the leg drag pass, organised as a complete study: overview, entry concepts, entries by turning the hips and using the stack, other entries, the concepts and mechanics of finishing, following up with other passes when the drag fails, mid-stage and end-stage troubleshooting, and a conclusion with narrated rolling. The instructor isn't named in the files; the structure ('narrated rolling', troubleshooting by stage) resembles the Grapplers Guide / Lachlan Giles style.
Leg Drag.for: Passers who want a complete leg drag system.
sources: Based on the lesson titles; instructor not identified.

Loopchoke by Meregali.overview: Nicholas Meregali's gi loop choke course in 12 parts. It starts with gripping and the loop choke from bottom, the upper and lower body connection, and the loop choke from top. It then covers set-ups from specific situations: the knee cut and top half guard, closed guard, sit-up guard and the 'heist', lasso guard, the single leg and the over-under pass. It ends with a wrap-up and how opponents escape (spinning, posturing, head position).
Loopchoke by Meregali.for: Gi players at any level; the loop choke works from top and bottom.
key: Loop choke from bottom and top
Set-ups from passing, closed guard, sit-up guard, lasso and single leg

Mason Fowler Modern Rubber Guard - The N.overview: Mason Fowler (a 10th Planet black belt and ADCC veteran) updates the rubber guard in 30 lessons. Establishing Rubber Guard covers controlling posture in closed guard, the sit-up sweep, and getting rubber guard from half guard (including when the opponent weaves an arm through, and countering head control). Mastering the Triangle covers the entry and finishes (hooking the leg, arm across, triangle-kimura). Mastering the Omoplata is the longest section: basic finish, roll counter drills, crucifix, S-grip choke, armlock from top, rolling to a mounted triangle, forcing the sweep, butterfly hook variations, gogoplata and 'maso-plata'. Finishing From Top covers shoulder locks, the top shoulder clamp to triangle and from 3/4 mount.
Mason Fowler Modern Rubber Guard - The N.for: Flexible closed guard and half guard players in no-gi.
key: Getting to rubber guard from closed and half guard

Meregali 2 On 1 Guard.overview: Nicholas Meregali's gi course on using the 2-on-1 grip (both hands on one arm) from guard, in seven chapters: understanding the 2-on-1 (inside versus outside gripping, connecting the lower body, retention, the initial connection); half guard (knee lever, arm drag, scissor sweep, back take); butterfly guard (conventional, belt control, back take, outside gripping); sit-up versus kneeling opponents (triangle, back take, leg wrap); closed guard (pendulum and scissor sweeps, back take, armbar); against a standing opponent (going under the hips, deep De La Riva X, balloon and tripod sweeps, ankle pick, triangle, wrestle-up); and dealing with bad grips.
Meregali 2 On 1 Guard.for: Gi guard players who want one grip that works from every guard.
key: Sweeps from half, butterfly and closed guard

Meregali - Half Guard.overview: Nicholas Meregali on top half guard in the gi, 22 lessons: forcing half guard and controlling the hips, behaving against frames, splitting the upper and lower body, crossface and underhook choices, 3/4 mount from a collar grip and passing through it, far-side underhooks, tripoding, double unders, the shoelaces grip, and beating the common bottom variations (half butterfly, dog fight, lockdown, sit-up guard, lapel control). The last lessons cover going from mount, side control and the back into half guard, and 'motion versus backtracking'.
Meregali - Half Guard.for: Gi top players who end up in half guard and want a systematic pass.
key: Beating lockdown, dog fight and half butterfly

Nicholas Meregali Deep De La Riva X.overview: Nicholas Meregali's gi deep De La Riva / X guard course, 33 lessons. The first half is entries against standing and grounded opponents from many grips (near sleeve and ankle, far sleeve and ankle, collar and ankle, 2-on-1, spider guard, collar-and-sleeve, the berimbolo). After a concepts lesson come the sweeps (near and far sleeve variations, ankle traps, 2-on-1 into wrestle-ups and back takes, double control, collar control), staying safe while guarding, and three breakdowns.
Nicholas Meregali Deep De La Riva X.for: Gi open guard players who want a modern De La Riva X game.
key: Entries vs standing and grounded opponents

Nicholas Meregali Mount.overview: Nicholas Meregali's gi mount course, 23 lessons. It starts with understanding mount (low versus high posture, high versus low mount, body configuration), then building control in each combination, using underhooks and clips. It then covers passing into mount from half guard and side control and maintaining underhooks. The submissions are organised by how many underhooks you have: no underhooks (collar chokes with elbows out and in, back take, kimura and americana), one underhook (arm-in triangle, half S-mount) and double unders (smother choke, S-mount chokes and armbars). It finishes with backtracking.
Nicholas Meregali Mount.for: Gi top players who get to mount and want to stay there and finish.
key: High versus low mount and posture

POWER PASSING 2.0 - FFION DAVIES.overview: Ffion Davies' gi passing and top attack course, 38 lessons in five chapters. Chapter 1 approaches the guard with the bullfighter (toreando) and variations (pant grip, collar-pant, cross grip and collar), the half stack and the long step to a side switch. Chapter 2 is the knee cut (beating DLR hooks, side swipe, hip clamp, forcing half guard, half guard to knee cut or mount, beating the butterfly hook, the cradle knee cut) with the baseball bat and darce chokes off it. Chapter 3 beats DLR, lasso and spider guards with stack passing (stack to leg drag, stack to turtle flip, smash pass). Chapter 4 is side control attacks (clearing the inside arm, far-side armbar, kimura to tarikoplata, judo armbar, step-over choke). Chapter 5 is mount attacks (transition to mount, burrito mount, head and arm choke, mounted triangle, transition to the back, S-mount armbar).
POWER PASSING 2.0 - FFION DAVIES.for: Gi players who want a pressure passing game that flows into attacks.
key: Stack passing against DLR, lasso and spider
sources: Based on the chapter and lesson titles.

Shane Curtis - Goth Guard - The Grapple.overview: Shane Curtis' 'Goth Guard' from The Grapple Club, 18 lessons in three chapters. Chapter 1 is the front headlock from bottom: hip bump to guillotine, countering the pass with the arm-in guillotine, the high elbow 'suicide' guillotine. Chapter 2 is the reverse Z guard: chin strap to guillotine, anaconda or sweep, the Goth lock on passing and as a sweep, sweeping to the 'soul crusher' or head and arm, and the reverse arm triangle. Chapter 3 uses front headlock ideas to pass the Z guard, sit-up guard and closed guard.
Shane Curtis - Goth Guard - The Grapple.for: No-gi players who like front headlock attacks and want to use them from the bottom.

Submeta/K-Guard 1 - Entries.overview: Submeta's K guard series part 1 (about 1h 45m): overview, concepts and strategy, then entries into the K guard from closed guard, from the initial guard engagement, from reverse De La Riva, the knee shield and keymaster, and from guard retention. Ends with a conclusion.
Submeta/K-Guard 1 - Entries.for: No-gi open guard players starting the K guard.
key: Entries from closed guard, RDLR, knee shield and retention
sources: Submeta course; based on the lesson titles.

Submeta/K-Guard 2 - Kneeling and Upper B.overview: Submeta's K guard series part 2 (about 1h 25m): using the K guard against kneeling opponents and attacking the upper body from it, with a long offence lesson, troubleshooting and a conclusion.
Submeta/K-Guard 2 - Kneeling and Upper B.for: K guard players facing kneeling passers.
sources: Submeta course; based on the lesson titles.

Submeta/K-Guard 3 - Backside, Matrix, Sh.overview: Submeta's K guard series part 3 (about 1h 45m): concepts and strategy for backside entries, the 'pathways' through the matrix and backside 50/50, and the shallow K variation.
Submeta/K-Guard 3 - Backside, Matrix, Sh.for: K guard players moving into leg entanglements.
sources: Submeta course; based on the lesson titles.

Submeta/K Guard 4 - 70-30, Front-side, T.overview: Submeta's K guard series part 4 (about 1h 25m): the 70-30 position (the longest lesson), front-side K guard, troubleshooting, and drills with narrated rolling.
Submeta/K Guard 4 - 70-30, Front-side, T.for: K guard players refining their game.
sources: Submeta course; based on the lesson titles.

Submeta/Passing single X, butterfly Ashi.overview: Submeta course (about 1h 40m) on passing leg-entanglement guards safely: single leg X (with troubleshooting and a summary), butterfly ashi, X guard and reverse X guard, plus drills.
Submeta/Passing single X, butterfly Ashi.for: No-gi passers who get swept or leg-locked by SLX and X guard players.
sources: Submeta course; based on the lesson titles.
